question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's consolidated authority within the Chinese Communist Party, including dominance over the Central Military Commission and Politburo, underpins the 95% trader consensus that he will retain power through 2026. Structural factors such as the absence of term limits, elite loyalty mechanisms, and suppression of factional challenges have minimized visible succession pressures in recent months. This skin-in-the-game pricing reflects historical patterns of long-tenured leadership stability absent major disruptions. Realistic scenarios that could still shift outcomes include sudden health developments, unexpected elite defections amid economic strains, or external crises forcing internal realignments before the end of the year.

eventMetadata.context_description: **A crowded 2028 Democratic field remains wide open nearly two years before the first primaries, with no candidate having formally declared and trader consensus reflecting fragmented support.** Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez holds the top position in prediction markets after gains in early-state polling, including leads in New Hampshire surveys, driven by her profile among progressives and refusal to rule out a bid while prioritizing midterms. Jon Ossoff and Gavin Newsom sit close behind, buoyed by Ossoff’s reelection fundraising and national buzz despite his repeated denials of interest, and Newsom’s established visibility from gubernatorial actions. Kamala Harris leads some national polls but trails in markets. The tightness stems from competing lanes—progressive energy, Senate and gubernatorial records, and name recognition—plus uncertainty over post-midterm positioning, potential endorsements, and early-state calendar effects that could shift probabilities once candidates commit.
